contents.name: Remark 1.9, passage through a kernel quotient
contents.support: If Z normal in I and Z≤kerρ, then P(gz)=P(g)ρ(z)=P(g), so P descends to I/Z and remains associated to N/Z. Include this elementary naturality check inline.

sources.title: Tammo tom Dieck, Representation Theory (2009)
sources.locator: §1.6 printed p.20 through Proposition 1.6.1 proof p.21; §4.2.5–4.2.7 printed p.57; §4.3 Problem 1 printed p.59

contents.name: Cyclic character group paragraph
contents.support: Use λ_k(r)=exp(2πik/n); orbit/stabilizer calculation is local.

contents.name: Products of character groups and duality for finite abelian groups
contents.reason: The full dual-group isomorphism and finite-abelian decomposition are not needed: the split theorem proves degree one by Schur and the dihedral example only uses cyclic characters.

contents.name: Proposition 1.6.1 and proof
contents.support: The product λ(a)β(h) is checked directly with the source semidirect convention.

contents.name: Problem 1, quaternion generators and matrices
contents.support: Take the quaternion subgroup; use Y equal to the negative of the printed second generator. Quotient factor is explicitly derived locally.

contents.name: Problem 1, binary tetrahedral nonmonomial group
contents.reason: The extension by C3 and its failure to be monomial belong to the subsequent M-group boundary examples, not the quaternion obstruction calculation.

contents.name: Theorem 1.2.2, positive-characteristic refinement
